text: Traditional amasi sours on the milk's own flora, in a smoked calabash or skin bag, for one to five days; lactococci dominate, with Leuconostoc and lactobacilli. Commercial amasi (per the Wikipedia article, secondary figures) adds skim milk powder and gelatine, pasteurises, and sets with a Lactococcus lactis starter. The species list is from a background statement in Todorov 2008 citing a South African traditional-fermented-milk reference.
